title: The farewell tawaf
hook: a last circling before leaving Mecca

segments.voice: Yesterday: the days of tashriq, days of eating, drinking and remembering God at Mina. Your line: eat and remember.

People are already leaving. The rites are done, the days at Mina are over, and pilgrims are heading off in every direction, home to wherever home is. Ibn Abbas remembers the moment. The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ stops them with a sentence: none of you should leave until the last thing you do is at the House. Not the last purchase, not the last meal. The House. So before the road home, there's one more walk around the Ka'ba. Today, the farewell tawaf.
screen: `LEAVING IN EVERY DIRECTION.` → `NONE OF YOU SHOULD LEAVE…` → `…UNTIL THE LAST THING IS THE HOUSE.`

segments.voice: First, the rule. Ibn Abbas's report, in Sahih Muslim, is simple: let the last of your time be at the House. A pilgrim's stay ends where it began, circling the Ka'ba. Second, the exception. In another report from Ibn Abbas, in Sahih al-Bukhari, people were commanded to make their last act at the House, except that it was lightened for a woman on her period. She may set out without it. Two days ago, Safiyyah's story showed which circling couldn't be skipped. This is the one that could be lifted. Third, how the schools weigh it. Some schools of law hold the farewell tawaf to be required of pilgrims leaving Mecca, so that missing it calls for an offering. Others hold it to be strongly recommended. Each school reads the same reports, and each has its reasons. Fourth, the word itself. Wada' means a farewell. Tradition calls the Prophet's own pilgrimage, the one these lessons have been following, the Farewell Pilgrimage, Hajjat al-Wada', and he did not make another. You met that pilgrimage back on day two hundred eighty-four. So two goodbyes fold together here: a pilgrim's goodbye to the House, and the memory of the Prophet's goodbye to his people. What the rite teaches is a way of leaving. Not slipping out the side door. Not letting the last memory be a crowded shop or a line for the bus. Going back to the center once more, and leaving from there, with the place you're leaving as the last thing you saw.
screen: `LET THE LAST OF IT BE AT THE HOUSE.` · `LIGHTENED FOR A WOMAN ON HER PERIOD.` · `REQUIRED, OR STRONGLY RECOMMENDED.` · `WADA': A FAREWELL.` · then, large: `GOODBYE TO THE HOUSE.`

segments.voice: Think of a goodbye that's coming, the end of a job, a friend moving, a visit with a parent that ends on Sunday, or one you rushed in a parking lot or a text. Picture how you'd want that last moment to go, who you'd look at and what you'd say. If you pray, hold that person in your du'a; if not, simply hold them in mind.
The farewell tawaf. The last circling of the Ka'ba before a pilgrim leaves Mecca, so the final act of the journey is at the House. Today's word.
Your line: goodbye to the house. The way you leave is part of the visit. Go well.

howItsDone: Before leaving Mecca, pilgrims circle the Ka'ba one last time in the farewell tawaf; women on their period are excused from it, and the schools differ on whether it is required or strongly recommended.

options: The report commands it, but lightens it for a woman on her period.
Yes, and anyone who misses it has to come back and redo the Hajj.
No. It's only for pilgrims who missed the circling after the sacrifice.

notes: Muslim 1327 (Ibn Abbas): people leaving in every direction; 'none of you should depart until his last act is at the House'. Confirm.
Bukhari 1755 (Ibn Abbas; also Muslim 1328): commanded, lightened for the menstruating woman. Confirm.
